You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like mid-2020. Unemployment is at its maximum z-score, payrolls are deeply negative, and industrial production is very weak, which fits April–June 2020. The details narrow it further.

- The 3-month change in the 10-year yield is +1.0, and Treasury 20y+ 3-month returns are -2.5. That pattern suggests yields are rising from a trough, so the March 2020 low in yields has passed.
- Equities are up for the month (+2.5) but down over 3, 6 and 12 months, which suggests the end of March or April 2020. The 12-month equity return of -2.0 is odd for April 2020, though the z-score is measured against a 36-month window.
- The 3-month change in the policy rate is +0.5 and its level is -1.5. That is a strange combination, because the rate was cut to zero in March 2020. Against the prior 36 months, which included rates of about 2%, a near-zero rate would sit at a low z-score.
- The 3-month change in unemployment is +3.0, so the jump has been recent. Unemployment in April 2020 was 14.7%, a very large jump from February.
- Investment-grade credit has a 6-month return of +3.0 and a 3-month return of -1.0. That implies the March crash is inside the 3-month window, which points to May or June 2020.
- The Baa spread is +2.0, down 0.5 over 3 months, which is consistent with April–May 2020 after the March peak.
- The VIX is +1.5, which fits May 2020.
- Headline CPI at -2.0 fits May 2020.
- US equity 12-month return of -2.0 doesn't fit May 2020, when the S&P was roughly +12% on the year. The z-scoring may explain it, though.
- Equities up 2.5 for the month with a 3-month change of -0.5 fits April 2020, which had a 3-month return of about -13% and a 1-month return of +13%. May would show a 3-month return near -5%.
- The 10-year 3-month change of +1.0 doesn't fit April 2020 well, since the 10-year was at 0.6% in April versus 1.9% in January. May is also unlikely to fit. Treasury 20y+ with a 3-month return of -2.5 is odd for either month.

Overall, the best fit is May 2020, with April 2020 a close alternative.
